newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMB sees steady outlook after strong 1996.
newsitem.headline: AMB sees steady outlook after strong 1996.

text.p: German insurer Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs AG (AMB) on Friday forecast satisfactory growth and earnings in the current year, after its net profit rose some 30 percent in 1996.

"The group expects satisfactory growth overall for the current year...If capital markets develop favourably one could expect that the group net profit will be satisfactory again," the group said in a mandatory statement.
AMB reported group net profit of around 340 million marks for 1996, around 30 percent up from the previous year and said its earnings per share should also show strong growth.
That should allow it to raise its dividend to 16 marks from 15 marks, AMB said. With the customary tax credit, that will bring the total per-share payout to 22.85 marks.
Profit growth in 1996 was primarily driven by successful restructuring measures and high profits at foreign units, particularly in the Netherlands, AMB said.
Total group sales reached just under 20 billion marks, a rise of 6.5 percent, of which insurance accounted for 17 billion marks, up from 16.2 billion the previous year.
AMB said its life insurance business had developed especially well, with premium income up 4.9 percent to 9.3 billion marks from 8.8 billion, which it said was better than the market average.

German insurance companies have been plagued by weak sales growth in recent years. Germany's persistent economic slowdown and fierce price competition, especially in non-life segments, has been a major factor.
Earlier this month, German market leader Allianz AG Holding reported a six percent rise in premium income for 1996 to 74.7 billion marks, amid a mere 1.4 percent rise in life and health premiums.
AMB's German premiums rose 4.4 percent while foreign premiums rose 9.7 percent, to which AMB said its Dutch units had contributed most.
Group capital investments rose seven percent to more than 73 billion marks.
The group's mortgage business, its Badenia Bausparkasse unit, extended its market share in 1996 and is also expected to improve its profits, AMB said.
Badenia's net new business rose more than 31 percent to nearly 8.2 billion marks.
